title: Leveraging Dual Output LUTs with Pipelining for Efficient BCD to Binary Converter on FPGA
problem: Embedded systems often use BCD (binary-coded decimal) format for decimal representation, but binary arithmetic requires conversion to binary format. Traditional converters have suboptimal FPGA resource utilization.
motivation: BCD-to-binary conversion is common in human-centric and embedded applications. Efficient FPGA implementation using architecture-specific primitives (dual-output LUTs) can improve throughput and resource utilization.
method: Parallel and pipelined BCD-to-binary converter architectures using FPGA-specific dual-output LUTs and carry chains. Primitive instantiation for direct FPGA optimization.
key_novelty: Dual-output LUT and pipelined design achieving good speed-area tradeoffs for BCD-to-binary conversion with optimized FPGA primitive utilization.
contributions: Parallel converter architecture using dual-output LUTs
Addition tree optimization for converter design
limitations: Abstract provides limited quantitative results. No specific throughput (MHz), area (LUTs), or latency numbers provided. Comparison details with existing designs not given.
primary_theme: FPGA arithmetic optimization for embedded systems
